questions.q: The letters of the word 'MANKIND' are written in all possible orders and arranged in serial order as in an English dictionary. Then the serial number of the word 'MANKIND' is _____ .
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
M A N K I N D

Arranging the letters alphabetically, we get

ADIKMNN

When the word starts with any of the letters A/D/I/K, the number of possibilities=6!2!×4=1440

Now when the word starts with MA, then the number of possibilities=4!2!×3=36

Now when the word starts with MAN, then the number of possibilities=3!×2=12

Now when the word starts with MANK, then the number of possibilities=4

Hence, rank of the work MANKIND is 1492

questions.q: The number of permutations, of the digits <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>7</mn></math> without repetition, which neither contain the string <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>153</mn></math> nor the string <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2467</mn></math>, is _______ .
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

The number 1,2,3,....,7

Now total numbers of 7 digit number will be 7! without repetition,

Now total numbers which contain string 154 will be 5!

Total numbers which contain string 2367 will be 4!

And number which contain both string 2367 & 154 will be 2

So, total number which does not contain string 154 or 2367 will be 7!-5!+4!-2

=5040-120+24-2

=5040-142=4898

Hence this is the required answer.

questions.q: The total number of two digit numbers <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>'</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>'</mo></math>, such that <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mn>3</mn><mi>n</mi></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mn>7</mn><mi>n</mi></msup></math> is a multiple of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn></math> , is ___ .
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
∵7n=(10-3)n=10k+(-3)n

7n+3n=10k+(-3)n+3n

10k+-3n+3n=10k if n=odd10k+2.3n if n=even

Let n=2t; t∈N

∴3n=32t=(10-1)t

=10p+(-1)t

.=10p±1

∴ if n= even then 7n+3n will not be multiply of 10

So if n is odd then only 7n+3n will be multiply of 10

∴n=11,13,15,……….,99

∴ Number of odd two digit numbers =45

questions.q: The number of ways of giving 20 distinct oranges to 3 children such that each child gets at least one orange is _____
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

We have to distribute 20 identical oranges to 3 children,

Let children A get OA oranges, children B gets OB oranges and children C gets OC oranges,

So, OA+OB+OC=20

Now this can be distributed using the multinomial theorem,

So, Number of ways will be,

=coefficient of x20 in x+x2+….+x183

=coefficient of x20 in x31+x+x2+….x173

=coefficient of x17 in 1-x181-x3

=coefficient of x17 in (1-x)-3

=C219=171

As we know that expansion of (1-x)-3 is 1+C13x+C24x2+C35x3+......+C1719x17........∞

Note: This is bonus question as here 20 oranges are considered identical but in question it is considered distinct.

questions.q: The total number of words (with or without meaning) that can be formed out of the letters of the word "DISTRIBUTION" taken four at a time, is equal to ______.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

Word 'DISTRIBUTION'

Now, we have III, TT, D, S, R, B, U, O, N

Number of words with 3 alike letter and 1 different will be,

=8C1×4!3!=32

Number of words with 2 alike and other 2 alike will be,

=4!2!2!=6

Number of words with 2 alike and 2 different will be,

=2C1×8C2×4!2!=672

Number of words with all different letters will be,

=9C4×4!=3024

Therefore, the total number of ways will be,

=3024+672+6+32

=3734

questions.q: In an examination, there are <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn></math> multiple choice questions with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn></math> choices, out of which exactly one is correct. There are <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn></math> marks for each correct answer, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></math> marks for each wrong answer and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn></math> mark if the question is not attempted. Then, the number of ways a student appearing in the examination gets <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn></math> marks is _____
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let the marks obtained in each of the five MCQ be x1, x2, x3, x4, x5

Now, x1+x2+x3+x4+x5=5

Only one possibility satisfies the above equation i.e. 3,3,3,-2,-2

Hence, total number of ways =5!3!2!×2×2=40

questions.q: Let b1b2b3b4 be a 4-element permutation with bi∈ 1,2,3,………,100 for 1≤i≤4 and bi≠bj for i≠j, such that either b1, b2, b3 are consecutive integers or b2,b3,b4 are consecutive integers. Then the number of such permutations b1b2b3b4 is equal to ______.

questions.solution:
bi∈1,2,3………100

Let A= set when b1 b2 b3 are consecutive

nA=97+97+……+97 added 98 times=97×98=9506

Similarly when b2 b3 b4 are consecutive

nB=97×98=9506

Now when b1 b2 b3 b4 are consecutive then nA∩B=97

questions.q: The sum of all the elements in the set <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>{</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mo>{</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>100</mn><mo>}</mo><mo>∣</mo></math> H.C.F. of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>n</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2040</mn></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn></math>} is equal to __________.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
The prime factorisation of the given number is 2040=23×3×5×17

The H.C.F. of n and 2040 is 1 if n is not a multiple of 2, 3, 5 and 17.

Hence n cannot be multiple of 2,3,5 and 17

Then sum is n(1)-(n(2)+n(3)+n(5)+n(17)-n(6)-n(10)-n(34)-n(15)-n(51)-n(85))+n(30))
Where n(a) means the sum of all numbers belonging to the set {1,2,…….100} which are divisible by a

=100×1012-2×50×512+3×33×342+5×20×212+17×5×62-6×16×172-10×10×112-34×2×32-15×6×72-51-85+180

=5050-2550-1683-1050-255+816+550+102+315+51+85-180

=1251

Alternate Solution:
Thus, the sum of all the required numbers taking the common elements only once, is 1+3+5+…..+99-3+9+15+21+……+99-5+25+35+55+65+85+95-17

Now, using the sum of n terms of an arithmetic progression i.e. Sn=n2a+l, where a is the first term and l is the last term.

=5021+99-1723+99-365-17

=502100-172102-365-17

=2500-867-365-17

=1251.

questions.q: Number of integral solutions to the equation <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>21</mn></math>, where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>4</mn></math>, is equal to _____ .
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
We have,

x≥1, y≥3, z≥4

⇒x-1≥0, y-3≥0, z-4≥0

So,

x+y+z=21

⇒x-1+y-3+z-4=13

So, number of non-negative integral solutions is

=C3-113+3-1=C215=15×142=105

where $\mathrm{a} \& \mathrm{~b}$ are co-prime numbers also since $m \& n$ are 2 digit nos, so
$10 \leq \mathrm{m} \leq 99 \& 10 \leq \mathrm{n} \leq 99$
i.e. $2 \leq \mathrm{a} \leq 16 \& 2 \leq \mathrm{b} \leq 16$
( $\because$ a is integer)
Now
$2 \leq \mathrm{a} \lt \mathrm{b} \leq 16 \& \quad \mathrm{a} \& \mathrm{~b}$ are co-prime
$\therefore$ if
$\mathrm{a}=2, \mathrm{~b}=3,5,7,9,11,13,15$
$a=3, b=4,5,7,8,10,11,13,14,16$
$a=4, b=5,7,9,11,13,15$
$a=5, b=6,7,8,9,11,12,13,14,16$
$\mathrm{a}=6, \mathrm{~b}=7,11,13$
$\mathrm{a}=7, \mathrm{~b}=8,9,10,11,12,13,15,16$
$\mathrm{a}=8, \mathrm{~b}=9,11,13,15$
$a=9, b=10,11,13,14,16$
$\mathrm{a}=10, \mathrm{~b}=11,13$
$\mathrm{a}=11, \mathrm{~b}=12,13,14,15,16$
$\mathrm{a}=12, \mathrm{~b}=13$
$a=13, b=14,15,16$
$\mathrm{a}=14, \mathrm{~b}=15$
$\mathrm{a}=15, \mathrm{~b}=16$
64 ordered pairs

questions.q: The number of words, with or without meaning, that can be formed using all the letters of the word ASSASSINATION so that the vowels occur together, is _____ .
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
In the word ASSASSINATION, we will treat all the vowels that is AAAIIO  as one letter only.

Now, we have AAAIIOSSSSNNT

This has 8=(7 + 1) letters of which S occurs 4 times, and N occur 2 times,

Thus, the number of ways of  arranging these letters =8!4!2!=840.

Now, 6 vowels in which A occurs 3 times, and I occur two times, they can be arranged in 6!3!2!=60  ways. 

 Therefore, required number of ways= (840 × 60) = 50400.

questions.q: The number of ways, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>16</mn></math> identical cubes, of which <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>11</mn></math> are blue and rest are red, can be placed in a row so that between any two red cubes there should be at least <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn></math> blue cubes, is ______.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given, 4 blue & 5 red spherical ball

Now according to question there should be minimum 2 blue ball in between any two red ball.

So assume a,b,c,d,e,f are number of blue balls,

So, a+b+c+d+e+f=11  ......(i)

Where b,c,d,e⩾2

Now let b=b'+2

c=c'+2

d=d'+2

e=e'+2

So equation (i) becomes

a+b'+2+c'+2+d'+2+e'+2+f=11

⇒ a+b'+c'+d'+e'+f=3

Now total ways will be

= 3+6-1C6-1=8C5=8C3=56

questions.q: If the digits are not allowed to repeat in any number formed by using the digits <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>6</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>8</mn><mo>,</mo></math> then the number of all numbers greater than <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>000</mn></math> is equal to __________.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
We have to form a number greater than 10,000 by using the digits 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, hence, the first place of the number can't be zero.

Thus, for the first place we have 4 choices i.e. 2, 4, 6, 8 and the remaining places can be filled with any of the digits, thus we have respectively 4, 3, 2, 1 choices.

Hence, using the fundamental principle of multiplication, the total numbers which are greater than 10,000 are

=4×4×3×2=96.

questions.q: The number of seven digit positive integers formed using the digits 1,2,3 and 4 only and sum of the digits equal to 12 is_______.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
The given numbers are 1,2,3,4 and sum of digits should be 12.

Case 1: 4 3 1 1 1 1 1 ,Here the sum of the digits is 12.

The number of ways arranging them is =7!5!=42.

Case 2: 4 2 2 1 1 1 1.

The number of ways arranging them is =7!2!4!=105

Case 3: 3 2 2 2 1 1 1.

The number of ways arranging them is =7!3!3!=140

Case 4: 3 3 2 1 1 1 1.

The number of ways arranging them is =7!2!4!=105

Case 5: 2 2 2 2 2 1 1

The number of ways arranging them is =7!5!2!=21

The total number of ways are =42+105+140+105+21

=413

Therefore, the required answer is 413.
